body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 17, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a high near 99° and air quality at a moderate 55. Overnight, a group of juveniles with a firearm on Monterey Street was the headline call. Grab your coffee and let’s catch up on the night, the news, and the week ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came around 11 p.m., when a group of five juveniles — one of whom pointed a firearm at the reporting party — was reported on Monterey Street. All were described as wearing dark clothing, and no shots were fired on the air as units responded. Earlier in the evening, shortly before 9:40 p.m., a possible shots-fired incident had units checking local hospitals for gunshot victims and searching for a suspect vehicle, though the exact location was unclear on the air. Fire crews also handled a one-acre grass fire with a slow rate of spread near the bike path off Oak Street just after 10:30 p.m., while officers worked a domestic violence call in progress on Animas Court at 9:54 p.m. and responded to a report of an ex-boyfriend smashing a vehicle windshield with a shotgun in the FoodMaxx parking lot on Ming Avenue around 11:03 p.m. The night also included a possible burglary at a Manhattan Drive residence, where a sliding back door was found shattered, and a vehicle fire inside a tow yard, though the exact location was unclear on the air. The small hours ran quieter, with the usual spread of disturbances, medical aids, and welfare checks.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 99° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 86° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and the National Weather Service has issued a Lake Wind Advisory for Lake Isabella until 8:00 p.m. this evening. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 55. No active fires are currently reported in the county.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** five vehicles were impounded during a recent checkpoint and saturation patrol in northwest Bakersfield. The operation, aimed at curbing dangerous driving and vehicle violations, resulted in multiple citations and the impoundment of vehicles for various infractions. The story highlights the ongoing efforts by local law enforcement to keep roads safe.

**According to 23ABC,** Robert F. Kennedy Jr. toured Bakersfield’s Edible Schoolyard Kern County program last week, praising it as a model that could reshape how schools across the country teach children about food and nutrition. The program, which brings gardening and cooking into the school curriculum at three Kern County campuses, connects classroom learning to what ends up on students’ plates. Kennedy emphasized that the program’s focus on fresh food and hands-on learning is working, with testing scores 15 points ahead of peer schools, and he believes it should be expanded nationally.

**KGET 17 told us that** Kern County Sheriff’s Office deputies arrested four individuals on various gun and drug possession charges following a copper wire theft investigation. The arrests underscore the ongoing challenges of property crime and illegal firearm possession in the county, and law enforcement’s efforts to address them.

## Something good

In a bright spot for the community, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recently visited Bakersfield to tour Edible Schoolyard Kern County, a program he believes could become a model for how schools across the country teach children about food, health, and nutrition. The program, which brings gardening and cooking into the school curriculum at three local campuses, connects classroom learning to what ends up on students’ plates. Kennedy’s visit and praise highlight the positive work being done in our community to improve children’s education and health.

## Coming up this week

This week brings several public meetings and events worth noting. On Tuesday, August 18, the Historic Preservation Commission meets at 4:00 p.m., followed by the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee at 12:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. Looking ahead to Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. And for entertainment, the Fox Theater has a busy schedule: Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio perform on August 22; Rodney Carrington takes the stage on August 27; CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE is on August 28; Willie Barcena performs on August 29; and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix is also on August 29. Finally, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA comes to the Fox on September 4.
